name: What accessibility features should be planned into an in-law suite?

mainEntity.name: What accessibility features should be planned into an in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Accessibility upgrades should be decided during the initial design phase to ensure doors, hallways, and bathrooms accommodate mobility changes over time. Prioritize wider doorways and zero-threshold entryways connecting the suite to the main home and exterior. In the bathroom, design a barrier-free, curbless walk-in shower with integrated wall backing for secure grab bars, built-in shower benches, and slip-resistant flooring. Comfort-height vanities, rocker-style light switches, and single-handle plumbing faucets also simplify everyday tasks. Incorporating these Universal Design elements during rough framing and plumbing prevents the need for invasive, costly remodels in the future.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan for wider doorways, zero-threshold entries, curbless walk-in showers with grab-bar backing, comfort-height vanities, and slip-resistant flooring from the start.
